medical.jointBackIssues: Lower back tightness from long study sessions
medicalPrecautions: Lower Back Protection: Heavy spinal axial compression and weighted bending avoided.
Plant-Based Optimization: High-bioavailability legumes, oats, and nut proteins prioritized.

baselineRoutine.title: Stress-Relief Bodyweight Foundation
baselineRoutine.examFriendlyNotes: Designed to be performed in 35 minutes to clear mental fog without inducing excessive fatigue before exams.
baselineRoutine.medicalClearanceNotes: Focuses on neutral spine alignment and low-impact movements to alleviate lower back tightness from sedentary study postures.

exercises.name: Bird-Dog
exercises.postureFocus: Keep back flat like a table, do not arch
exercises.medicalSafetyNote: Strengthens stabilizers without loading the spine

exercises.name: Glute Bridges
exercises.postureFocus: Squeeze glutes at the top, avoid hyperextending lower back
exercises.medicalSafetyNote: Safe for lower back as it avoids vertical compression

exercises.name: Wall Push-Ups
exercises.medicalSafetyNote: Reduces strain on shoulders and lower back compared to floor push-ups

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squats (to chair)
exercises.medicalSafetyNote: Chair provides a depth limit to protect knees

scaledRoutine.title: Restorative Deload Routine
scaledRoutine.examFriendlyNotes: Shortened 18m routine to prevent CNS burnout during exams/stress
scaledRoutine.medicalClearanceNotes: Focuses on mobility, stress relief, and gentle posture recovery

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
exercises.postureFocus: Move with the breath, slow controlled motion
exercises.medicalSafetyNote: Gentle on joints and relieves lumbar stiffness

exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold
exercises.postureFocus: Hinge at hips, keep spine long
exercises.medicalSafetyNote: Avoids rounding the lower back excessively
